privacy_modal.title: AI privacy notice
privacy_modal.intro: Memlore can use three kinds of AI providers. Local models keep your entries on your computer. Subscription CLIs and hosted APIs may send entry text to external services. Please review how each kind handles your data before continuing with a non-local provider.
privacy_modal.local_title: Local model — stays on your computer
privacy_modal.local_description: Your entries are sent to a server running on your own machine (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, …). Nothing leaves the computer; no network upload.
privacy_modal.subscription_title: Subscription CLI — uses your Claude / ChatGPT plan
privacy_modal.subscription_description: Memlore hands your prompt to a local CLI (claude / codex) you have signed in to. The CLI then forwards it to Anthropic or OpenAI under your subscription. Memlore never sees your API key, and AI calls count against your plan quota.
privacy_modal.remote_title: External / hosted model — entries leave your computer
privacy_modal.remote_description: Your entries are uploaded to a hosted provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Voyage, …) over HTTPS. The provider receives the entry text plus any query you make. Their privacy policy and the terms of your account apply to that data.
privacy_modal.scope_footnote: You only need to accept this notice once. After that, every non-local provider and every multi-entry AI feature is covered — including switching between hosted APIs and subscription CLIs.
privacy_modal.bullet_remote_text: Decrypted entry text is sent to the provider so it can answer your request.
privacy_modal.bullet_remote_query: Search query strings and image prompts also leave your device.
privacy_modal.bullet_remote_log: The provider may log requests indefinitely per their terms of service.
privacy_modal.bullet_remote_cache: Generated embeddings are cached locally so subsequent searches don't repay the cost.
privacy_modal.bullet_local_loop: Requests stay inside your computer — no internet round-trip.
privacy_modal.bullet_local_server: The local server you configured handles all inference.
privacy_modal.bullet_local_cache: Generated embeddings are cached locally so subsequent searches don't recompute.
privacy_modal.bullet_subscription_cli: Memlore spawns the {{cli}} CLI as a subprocess. The CLI reuses its own login (run `claude /login` / `codex login` once); Memlore never sees an API key.
privacy_modal.bullet_subscription_upstream: The CLI then sends your prompt to {{upstream}}'s servers as if you typed it in the CLI yourself. {{upstream}}'s privacy policy and the terms of your subscription apply.
privacy_modal.bullet_subscription_quota: AI features count against your subscription quota — the same as if you used the CLI directly.
privacy_modal.bullet_subscription_tools: Memlore disables CLI tools (filesystem, shell, MCP). The model can only return text replies.

backfill.title: Embedding index
backfill.description: Powers Semantic Search, Emotion Suggestions, and using your entries in Daily Chat. Pause / Resume / Index now control the queue; Rebuild re-embeds everything from scratch (useful after changing models).
backfill.reindex_needed: Embedding model changed — re-index entries so semantic search and emotion suggestions use the new vectors.
backfill.rebuild_confirm_body: This wipes existing vectors for the current model and re-embeds every entry from scratch. It may take a while, and with a hosted provider it will call that provider again for every entry.
backfill.status_waiting_help: After you stop editing, indexing waits a few minutes so continuous typing does not re-embed repeatedly. Only changed chunks are re-embedded. Use “Index now” to skip the wait.
backfill.status_stuck: Some entries are stuck — Index now re-queues them

embedding_decision.title: Embedding sync needs a decision
embedding_decision.intro: Another device uses a different embedding model or this device cannot index yet. Choose what to do — Memlore will not re-embed silently (that can spend API tokens). Pause stops re-embedding what other devices sent; new local edits keep indexing.
embedding_decision.reason_model_mismatch: Peer devices have vectors for a different model. Adopted vectors only work when the model matches yours.
embedding_decision.reason_missing_key: The embedding provider is configured but its API key is missing on this device. Keys never sync.
embedding_decision.reason_invalid_key: The embedding provider rejected the API key on this device. Check or re-enter it in Settings.
embedding_decision.reason_unconfigured: No embedding provider is configured on this device, so pending work cannot run.
embedding_decision.pause_keeps_local: New local edits keep indexing. Only peer-mismatch re-embed is paused.
embedding_decision.needs_key_hint: That model needs an API key on this device. Open AI settings to add it, then try again.
embedding_decision.error_select_peer: Select a peer model before switching.

background.title: Background indexing
background.description: Keeps the embedding index up to date as you write. After you stop editing, it waits a few minutes before indexing so continuous typing does not re-embed repeatedly. Only changed chunks are re-embedded — unchanged text is skipped.
background.consent_body: Background indexing will call your configured hosted provider to embed new and edited entries as you write. This uses your API quota, and cost scales with how many entries you write and how long they are — unchanged text is skipped.
background.protected_description: Off by default. When on, background indexing also embeds your locked entries. Invisible entries are always excluded.
background.protected_risk_body: Vectors from these entries are stored (and synced) encrypted like everything else, but with a hosted provider the entry text is sent to that provider to compute them.
background.protected_benefit_body: Semantic Search and Daily Chat can then cover your locked entries too, not just those currently unlocked.
background.protected_read_note: Locked and invisible entries stay excluded from search results and from anything Daily Chat retrieves while they're locked or hidden — this setting only affects what gets embedded in the background.

embedding_explainer.help_aria: Learn how AI works in Memlore

opt_in.title: Off until you turn it on
opt_in.body: Every AI feature starts off. Nothing is sent anywhere until you connect a provider, accept the privacy notice when needed, and enable the features you want — each feature has its own toggle.

no_server.title: Memlore has no AI cloud
no_server.body: There is no Memlore AI server and no telemetry. You bring your own provider — on this device, a local server, a subscription CLI, or a hosted API key. Your journal stays encrypted on your device; AI only sees text you deliberately process.

locked.title: Locked & invisible entries
locked.body: Locked and invisible entries are excluded from AI by default. You can optionally include locked entries for embedding or memory; invisible entries are always excluded. Even if something was indexed while unlocked, it is not shown in search or chat while it is locked or hidden.

kinds.title: Four ways to run AI
kinds.body: On-device models download once and run fully offline. Local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, and similar) keep data on your machine. Subscription CLIs (Claude CLI, Codex CLI) use tools already signed in on your computer. Hosted APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, and others) send requests over the internet and may spend tokens.

slots.title: Separate slots for chat, images, and embeddings
slots.body: Chat/generation, image generation, and embedding are configured independently on the Models tab. You can chat with one provider and embed with another — for example a subscription CLI for chat and an on-device model for search.

writing.title: Writing helpers
writing.body: Title suggestions, Highlights, Go Deeper reflection prompts, Continue & Rewrite, multi-entry summaries, period reviews, theme insights, and image generation each make a request when you use them. They use the generation or image model and do not need the embedding index.

chat.title: Daily Chat
chat.body: A multi-turn conversation about your day. You can attach specific entries or date ranges, optionally pull related journal context when embeddings are set up, and use Memory & Persona so replies can draw on lasting facts about you. Conversations can be saved as journal entries.

retrieval.title: Meaning-based features
retrieval.body: Semantic Search, Emotion Suggestions, and journal context in Daily Chat need an embedding index — they match by meaning, not just keywords. Attaching a specific entry or date range in chat does not need embeddings; those are read directly.

what.title: What embeddings are
what.body: Embeddings turn journal text into vectors so Memlore can compare meaning locally. That local index powers Semantic Search, Emotion Suggestions, and optional journal context in Daily Chat. Details of how indexing runs live next to the embedding controls in Settings → AI.

background.title: Background indexing
background.body: While the app is open and indexing is allowed, a background worker keeps the index up to date as you write. Hosted embedding providers need an extra token-cost consent before background indexing runs. Pause, resume, index-now, and rebuild sit next to the embedding model in Settings.

when_sent.title: When text leaves this device
when_sent.body: Only when you use a hosted or subscription provider for a feature you trigger — or when hosted background indexing is on. On-device and local-server paths keep text on your machine. Changing a remote provider or endpoint re-prompts the privacy notice.

tokens.title: Tokens, usage & audit
tokens.body: Hosted providers may charge per call (chat, embeddings, images). On-device and local servers have no token cost. Statistics → AI Usage and Audit log show call metadata only — never the content of your entries.

response_language.label: AI response language
response_language.hint: Applies to every AI feature — title suggestions, highlights, Go Deeper, summaries, and more.

user_memory.master_toggle_description: When off, memories are not scanned, extracted, or used in Daily Chat.
user_memory.gen_model_quality_hint: Tip: pick a high-quality model here — it distills your entries into memories, merges duplicates, and builds your persona, so accuracy matters more than speed. It runs only on memory scans and persona rebuilds, not on every chat.

scan_help.title: How "Scan memories" works
scan_help.scan_body: Looks through recent journal entries and Daily Chat sessions for new or changed text, then queues those sources for extraction into short memory facts. This pass always runs when you press "Scan memories". The background worker also scans automatically on a short interval — scan is not limited to the button.
scan_help.tidy_body: Uses the memory generation model to merge duplicates, combine related fragments, and drop trivia across your whole memory list. Tidy only runs when you press "Scan memories" — the background worker does not tidy automatically. It is a separate cleanup pass, not the same as claiming new sources.
scan_help.cooldown_body: Tidy runs at most once every 6 hours. If you press "Scan memories" again inside that window, new sources are still claimed, but tidy is skipped. A skipped tidy does not reset the cooldown clock — only a real tidy advances it — so mid-window presses do not push the next tidy further out.
scan_help.last_scanned_body: The timestamp next to the memory count updates whenever a scan runs — both when you press "Scan memories" and when the background worker scans automatically. It does not mean the tidy pass ran.
scan_help.manage_body: Opens the full list so you can search, edit text, enable or disable items, or delete them. Pressing "Manage memories" does not start a scan or tidy.

user_memory.empty_state: No memories yet. Scan to extract notable facts from your entries.
user_memory.slot_missing_gen: Memory needs a generation model — pick one above.
user_memory.slot_missing_embed: Memory needs an embedding model — pick one above.
user_memory.feature_off_body: Configure both models (generation + embedding) for Memory to run.
user_memory.protected_description: Off by default. When on, locked entries become eligible for memory extraction and persona style sampling. Invisible entries are always excluded.
user_memory.protected_risk_body: Facts and writing style from these locked entries can still appear in your memories and persona.
user_memory.protected_risk_body_hosted_active: Facts and writing style from these locked entries can still appear in your memories and persona. Memory is on a hosted or CLI provider, so the full text of those entries is sent there too — not just short facts.
user_memory.protected_benefit_body: Memory extraction and Build Your Persona can then draw on your locked entries too, not just the ones currently unlocked.
user_memory.protected_read_note: Invisible entries are always excluded, whether this is on or off.
user_memory.hosted_active_indicator: Memory is running on a hosted or CLI provider — raw journal entries and chat transcripts are sent to it during extraction and persona building.
user_memory.hosted_confirm_title: Send your raw journal and chat data off this machine?
user_memory.hosted_confirm_body: Memory and persona send your raw journal entries and Daily Chat transcripts to the provider — not just short facts. That goes further than Daily Chat alone.
user_memory.hosted_confirm_body_protected_active: Memory and persona send your raw journal entries and Daily Chat transcripts to the provider — not just short facts. Locked entries are included, so their text leaves this machine too.
user_memory.hosted_confirm_footer: You can switch back to an on-machine provider at any time.

persona.title: Build Your Persona
persona.description: A profile used to help entry-writing features sound more like you.
persona.summary_empty: Not built yet — answer a few questions or rebuild from memories.
persona.needs_generation_model_title: Pick a chat model to use Persona
persona.needs_generation_model_body: Your persona is added to the AI's instructions when it writes for you, so it needs a chat model. Choose one in the Models tab.
persona.needs_generation_title: Connect your chat provider to use Persona
persona.needs_generation_body: Your persona is added to the AI's instructions when it writes for you. The chat model is chosen, but this device has no credential for its provider — add one in the Providers tab.
persona.needs_memory_slots_body: Your persona still works, but rebuilding it from your memories needs a generation and an embedding model. Pick them in the Memory tab.
persona.answers_empty: Answer a few questions to describe what you want your writing to sound like.
persona.not_enough_material_body: Add a few memories or entries, then rebuild your persona. You can also answer the questions now.
persona.not_enough_style_material_body: Add at least three eligible journal entries, then rebuild to generate a Writing style.
persona.rebuild_confirm_body: This will replace the Traits & preferences and Writing style sections you edited. Your answers will stay unchanged.

interview.title: Answer a few questions
interview.description: Every answer is optional. Your answers help entry-writing features follow your preferences from day one.
interview.privacy: These answers stay on this device. They are sent to a provider only when you use a feature that applies your persona.

preferred_name.label: What should the AI call you, and how should it address you?
preferred_name.help: For example: Minh, and use informal Vietnamese.

journal_goal.label: What do you mainly journal for?
journal_goal.help: Choose the closest fit, or leave it blank.

voice_preference.label: When the AI rewrites or continues your text, should it keep your voice as-is or polish it?

languages.label: Which language(s) do you write in, and do you mix them?
languages.help: Mention any language switching you want preserved.

three_words.label: Three words that describe you.
three_words.help: A few qualities, values, or moods are enough.

life_priorities.label: What matters most in your life right now?
life_priorities.help: People, projects, goals, or anything else important.

avoid_topics.label: Anything the AI should NOT bring up or speculate about?
avoid_topics.help: This is a hard preference for persona-based writing.

length_preference.label: How long should AI-written text be?
length_preference.help: Choose the default length you prefer.

persona.used_by: Used by Continue & Rewrite in the editor and Save as entry in Daily Chat — they write in your voice. Works independently of Memory.
persona.answers_description: Your own words about how the AI should write for you. These are authoritative — they win over anything generated.
persona.traits_description: A short profile of you, generated from your memories and answers. Edit it if something is off.
persona.style_description: How your writing sounds — sentence length, tone, language mixing. Generated from your entries.

user_memory.used_by: Used by Daily Chat — notable facts about you are retrieved and added to the conversation.
